content.text:
The chat input's tab bar now ends with a "Context" figure and a New Session button. I also finished the ribbon change from before, whose test updates had been cut off. All 226 tests pass (1 ignored), dev and release builds have no warnings, and the piton checks and build pass. I haven't looked at any of this in the running app or tried it against a real harness run.

**Context figure**
- It sits at the far right of the tab bar, after the help text, reading e.g. "Context 42.1k". Short forms go "850", "42.1k", "123k", "1.2M". Its tooltip gives the exact count.
- The number comes from the usage Claude Code reports with each reply. It counts everything the model was given (cached or not) plus what it wrote, as of the latest reply. Subagents' usage doesn't count.
- The Ask tab has its own conversation, so on Ask the figure is the questions' conversation; on the other tabs it's the tasks' conversation.
- It survives reopening a project: the figure is worked out again from the saved history of the conversation being resumed.
- It's a token count, not a percentage, because the harness doesn't report the model's context window size.

**New Session**
- It's a small ghost button with a sparkles icon.
- It drops the selected tab's conversation, so the next prompt starts fresh with nothing to resume, and the figure reads "Context 0".
- A run of the old conversation that's still going finishes as normal but can't bring it back, and neither can the project's history being reloaded. That lasts until the app is next opened, when the history's latest conversation is resumed as usual.
- It's disabled when there's no conversation to drop.

**Code:**
- `src/harness.rs` parses a new usage event.
- `src/prompt_mode.rs` keeps the context on each conversation, ignores runs started before New Session, and exposes `new_session`.
- `src/chat_input.rs` has the figure and the button.

**Tests:**
- The harness parser picks up usage and ignores subagents' usage.
- A conversation restored from history comes back with its latest context.
- The token labels read as above.
- A prompt-mode test clicks the real New Session button. It checks that the figure clears and nothing is resumed, and that a late report from the old run doesn't restore it. Removing the guard makes that last check fail.
- That prompt-mode test feeds session and usage events straight in rather than through a real harness run, so the wiring inside the actual run loops is checked by reading the code only.
- The help-text test now expects the help to fill the bar up to the figure, with New Session at the far right.

**Spec:**
- The ChatInput scope has a new session section describing the figure and the button.
- The harness integration scope describes leaving a conversation and how context is counted.

**Ribbon, finished:** a full button now grows to three slim buttons tall when the tallest column beside it is that tall (as on Spec), and stays two tall otherwise (as on Application). The tests and the RibbonScope spec say so.

One oddity: the piton check now reports 81 files where earlier runs said 106. No spec files are missing: git tracks 75 and all are on disk, so I think the old figure counted something else, but I haven't confirmed that.
